# ثـمـــن مــوتــرك — Apache settings

DirectoryIndex index.php index.html

# The site is open to search engines. Indexing is switched from the
# control panel (🔎 Google & search), which drives the robots meta tag
# and sitemap.xml — there is deliberately no X-Robots-Tag header here,
# because a header cannot be turned off from the panel.

# /sitemap.xml is generated by sitemap.php
<IfModule mod_rewrite.c>
  RewriteEngine On
  RewriteRule ^sitemap\.xml$ sitemap.php [L]
</IfModule>

# Uploads can be large — raise the limits (ignored on some hosts; use php.ini then)
<IfModule mod_php.c>
  php_value upload_max_filesize 64M
  php_value post_max_size 260M
  php_value max_file_uploads 20
  php_value max_execution_time 300
  php_value memory_limit 256M
</IfModule>

# Include-only files must never be opened directly
<FilesMatch "^(lib|config|content|concept|brand|carmap|legalpage|admin_content|admin_auth|seo|smtp|pdfdoc|arabic|arabic-forms)\.php$">
  Require all denied
</FilesMatch>

Options -Indexes

<IfModule mod_deflate.c>
  AddOutputFilterByType DEFLATE text/html text/css application/javascript application/json
</IfModule>

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Caching
#
# The PAGE must never be stored. index.php is what carries every change — new
# steps in the form, a new splash, new wording — and a phone that keeps
# yesterday's copy shows yesterday's site until somebody clears the cache by
# hand. iPhone Safari is the worst for this: with no rule at all it invents one.
#
# The FILES beside it can be kept for a long time, because their addresses now
# carry the moment the file was last changed — app.css?v=1786420329. That
# number is put there by the site itself (asset() in lib.php), so uploading a
# new app.css changes its address on its own and every phone fetches the new
# one without anybody clearing anything. Nothing is versioned by hand any more,
# which is why these files may be kept for a year instead of a week.
#
# sw.js is the exception and its rule comes last so it wins: the service worker
# is the file that decides what a phone keeps offline, so it must always be
# read fresh from the server.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
<IfModule mod_headers.c>
  <FilesMatch "\.(php|webmanifest)$">
    Header set Cache-Control "no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate, max-age=0"
    Header set Pragma "no-cache"
  </FilesMatch>
  # versioned files — safe to keep, the address changes when the file does
  <FilesMatch "\.(css|js|png|webp|jpg|jpeg|svg|woff2?)$">
    Header set Cache-Control "public, max-age=31536000"
  </FilesMatch>
  # the service worker itself, so a new version is always noticed — keep last
  <FilesMatch "^sw\.js$">
    Header set Cache-Control "no-cache, must-revalidate, max-age=0"
    Header set Pragma "no-cache"
    Header unset Expires
  </FilesMatch>
</IfModule>

<IfModule mod_expires.c>
  ExpiresActive On
  ExpiresByType text/html "access plus 0 seconds"
  ExpiresByType image/png  "access plus 1 year"
  ExpiresByType image/webp "access plus 1 year"
  ExpiresByType image/jpeg "access plus 1 year"
  ExpiresByType text/css  "access plus 1 year"
  ExpiresByType application/javascript "access plus 1 year"
</IfModule>

AddType application/manifest+json .webmanifest
